sentences.text: Doratodon was an extinct genus of crocodylomorph that lived during the Late Cretaceous. It is classified as an extinct genus of ziphodont crocodyliform from the Late Cretaceous.

This small-bodied ziphosuchian possessed a narrow but deep skull where the maxillae formed much of that depth. A defining antorbital fenestra, an opening located between the nostrils and the eye sockets, was present. The animal had a tall snout typical of sebecosuchians, with nostrils positioned at the tip of the rostrum that opened primarily upward and to the sides.

Doratodon was a relatively small animal possessing ziphodont teeth with flattened sides and serrated edges. It is known from diagnostic triangular teeth that are flattened side-to-side and finely serrated on the front and back edges, along with some fragmented jaw fragments.
Doratodon is a cosmopolitan genus found across various European countries that were part of an archipelago separated by the Tethys Sea during the Cretaceous.
Fossil evidence suggests this was a predatory animal that actively hunted, as evidenced by its triangular, serrated teeth.

The first remains of Doratodon were discovered by Eduard Suess in 1859 in a coal mine near Wiener Neustadt, Austria. Geologist Eduard Suess discovered the holotype fossil of Doratodon in 1859 at the Gute Hoffnung coal mine near Wiener Neustadt, Austria.
Emanuel Bunzel described the holotype mandible as Crocodilus carcharidens in 1871. Emanuel Bunzel originally named the type specimen Crocodylus carcharidens in 1871.
Harry Govier Seeley proposed the name Doratodon in 1881, initially classifying the material as a dinosaur. The genus Doratodon was named by Seeley in 1881.
It is suggested that Doratodon was a terrestrial animal, making it an outlier among the primarily aquatic neosuchians of the Cretaceous European fauna.
Reconstructed neurovasculature from an Italian specimen suggests Doratodon had somatosensory capabilities similar to semiaquatic taxa.

In the Csehbánya Formation, Doratodon coexisted with mosasaurs, lizards, multiple crocodilian relatives, turtles, pterosaurs, and various dinosaurs including ceratopsians, abelisaurids, and sauropods.

In the Grünbach Formation, Doratodon coexisted with pterosaurs, eusuchians, choristoderes, turtles, a tetanuran theropod, the rhadinodontid Mochlodon, and the nodosaurids Rhadinosaurus and Struthiosaurus.
In the Sierra Perenchiza Formation, Doratodon coexisted with crocodilian relatives, turtles, a caecilian, frogs, pterosaurs, an albanerpetontid, and various indeterminate dinosaurs.
Teeth from the Coniacian of Italy and the Maastrichtian of Romania are sometimes assigned to the genus Doratodon.
Phylogenetic analysis following the discovery of Doratodon ibericus confirmed the genus's relationship with sebecosuchians.
Doratodon lived from the Santonian to the Thanetian stages, approximately 85.7 to 56 million years ago.
Fossils of Doratodon are known from at least three European formations: Grünbach, Csehbánya, and Sierra Perenchiza.
Doratodon carcharidens fossils have been found in the Campanian Grünbach Formation of Austria, the Campanian Villaggio del Pescatore of Italy, and the Santonian Csehbánya Formation of Hungary.
Doratodon ibericus has only been found in the Campanian-aged Sierra Perenchiza Formation in Spain.
Doratodon has been classified variously as a dinosaur, goniopholid neosuchian, hsisosuchid, and sebecosuchian since its discovery.
Dalla Vecchia and Andrea Cau argue that isolated teeth found in Italy and Romania cannot be confidently assigned to Doratodon.
Éric Buffetaut suggested in 1979 that Doratodon was related to the Asian Hsisosuchus, but this hypothesis was refuted by Wu et al. in 1994.
Rabi and Sebök suggest that Doratodon was a true Late Cretaceous immigrant to Europe because no other ziphodont crocodyliforms are known from the continent prior to its appearance.
It is debated whether the ankylosaurian dinosaur Rhadinosaurus alcimus, known only from its holotype, is actually the same animal as Doratodon carcharidens.
Bergisuchus and Iberosuchus do not appear closely related to the Cretaceous Doratodon sebecosuchian found across Europe during the Upper Cretaceous.
